subject: mathematics
question_text: Eliminate θ from x = a cos³θ and y = b sin³θ.

mark_split.label: Write cos θ and sin θ as cube roots

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 17, book p.85. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards isolating cos θ and sin θ as cube roots first and applying cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 second, since the identity is what actually removes θ. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Checked numerically with a = 2.7, b = −1.4 and θ = 200°: x = −2.2403775571 and y = 0.0560122592, and (x/a)²⁄³ + (y/b)²⁄³ = 1.0000000000. Negative a, negative b and a third-quadrant θ were used on purpose, because a real cube root keeps the sign of its argument and so the relation carries no ± branch.

recall_prompt: Say how you would eliminate θ here — what you take from each equation, and which identity finishes it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write cos θ and sin θ as cube roots
steps.margin_note: First mark. Dividing needs a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0. A real cube root is unique, so cos θ and sin θ come out with no ± sign — unlike a square root.
steps.memory_tip: A real number has exactly one real cube root, so there is no ± sign here. Take the cube root of each ratio.
lines: Here a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0, so we may divide.
A real number has exactly one real cube root,

recall.must_convey: That each equation is divided by its constant and the cube root taken, giving cos θ = (x/a)¹⁄³ and sin θ = (y/b)¹⁄³.
accept: divide by a and by b then take the cube root of each side
cos theta is x by a to the power one third and sin theta is y by b to the power one third
take cube roots so there is no plus or minus
a tho, b tho divide chesi cube root teeskuntam
isolate cos cubed theta and sin cubed theta first

steps.why: Both equations are cubes, and a real cube root is unique, so each ratio gives the trigonometric ratio itself with no sign case. Dividing is only allowed because a and b are not zero.
common_mistakes: Writing a ± sign, which a cube root does not need.
Dividing by a and b without stating that they are not zero.

steps.label: Use cos²θ + sin²θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Squaring the two cube roots turns them into two-thirds powers, and cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 holds for every θ, so θ disappears.
steps.memory_tip: Square both cube roots and add. The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 is what removes θ.
lines: But cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 for every θ, so

recall.must_convey: That squaring both and adding gives (x/a)²⁄³ + (y/b)²⁄³ = 1 by cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.
accept: square both and add so you get x by a to the two thirds plus y by b to the two thirds equals one
use cos squared plus sin squared equals one
the answer is x over a power two by three plus y over b power two by three equals one
rendu square chesi add cheste one vastundi

steps.why: θ disappears because cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 holds for every θ. Squaring the two cube roots turns each into a two-thirds power, and the relation left between x and y is the answer.
common_mistakes: Adding the cube roots instead of their squares.
Writing (x/a)³ + (y/b)³ = 1, which is not what the identity gives.
